newsitem.title: CANADA: BHP says Canada mine illness cleared up.
newsitem.headline: BHP says Canada mine illness cleared up.

text.p: A mysterious illness that hit 50 workers at a Canadian diamond mine being built by Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd has cleared up and did not delay construction, company officials said on Friday.
"Basically we think it was the flu," BHP's BHP Diamonds Inc President James Rothwell told Reuters after the annual meeting of BHP's partner in the project, Dia Met Minerals Ltd.
"It didn't delay construction and we've had no further problems," Rothwell said.
Over a two-week period earlier this month, 50 of the 700 workers at the BHP-Dia Met site in Canada's Arctic for the country's first commercial diamond mine, were stricken with an unknown sickness.

Dia Met officials said the project was on schedule and on budget for a production start in the second half of 1998. Rothwell said production would initially be 200 million carats of diamonds a year, doubling to 400 million carats yearly through the mine's 25-year lifespan.
Dia Met President Jim Eccott said it was not yet decided who would market the diamonds, saying: "De Beers (Consolidated Mines Ltd is a possibility. We're in discussions with them.
"But we're still working on the marketing. We're also looking at a number of alternatives (to De Beers)," Eccott said.
